title: Septieme Solo de Concert Op. 93
identity: Jean-Baptiste Singelée, Septième Solo de Concert no. 7, Op. 93 (1863), originally for baritone saxophone and piano. The inspected public Musik Fabrik/Notendownload preview is a 2011 baritone edition revised by Paul Wehage, MFJBS011. Separate Roncorp and Dorn catalog leads also describe baritone editions. The current catalog’s alto/piano tag is not supported by these sources; the intended edition remains unresolved.

evidence.claim: CiNii identifies Roncorp c.1987, compiled/edited by Bruce Ronkin, baritone saxophone and piano, about 3:00, eight-page score and attached part. IMSLP independently lists Op. 93 for baritone saxophone and piano.
IMSLP lists Op. 93 as the 1863 Seventh Solo for baritone saxophone and piano, consistent with the CiNii catalog record.
Public product page identifies MFJBS011, a baritone saxophone and piano edition of Op. 93, with 12 pages and an approximately 3:30 duration; seller’s “medium” label is not used as a SaxoBrain level.
evidence.source_name: Musik Fabrik Music Publishing listing via Notendownload

evidence.claim: Public score-preview images visibly identify the edition as baritone saxophone and piano, Jean-Baptiste Singelée Op. 93, revised by Paul Wehage and © 2011 Editions de la Fabrique Musique. I inspected the opening and a later page.

score_observations.claim: The opening preview page marks “Introduction: Allegro risoluto”; the baritone saxophone begins with an ascending slurred figure and tied notes at forte, against a piano part with strongly accented chordal attacks.

A later preview page shows a contrast between the saxophone’s slurred/held melodic phrases and repeated chord patterns in the piano; a subsequent saxophone entry follows a rest with a quick connected figure. The selected previews do not establish the full range or complete form.

review_focus: Inference from the inspected baritone preview: consider slurred agility and tied-note breath planning against strongly articulated repeated piano chords. These observations apply to the previewed baritone edition, not a confirmed alto edition.
collection_flag: Original nineteenth-century saxophone contest solo. Cataloged Roncorp and Dorn edition leads identify baritone rather than alto; no evidence yet confirms an alto-specific adaptation.

score_links.description: Product page with 12-page edition and public preview images. Opening and later score pages were retrieved and visually inspected.

gaps: The assigned catalog entry specifies alto saxophone, while the original, Roncorp, Dorn, and inspected 2011 preview identify baritone saxophone; no alto adaptation has been confirmed.
Only selected public preview pages were inspected; full range and complete technical demands remain unknown.
No college/professional or pedagogical placement verified.

proposed_corrections.evidence: IMSLP, CiNii, and the inspected public 2011 score preview identify the original/previewed edition as baritone saxophone and piano. The intended entry-specific edition is unresolved, so verify before changing.
